claim: Let F be a finite union-closed family with empty set adjoined, let S be a minimum nonempty member of size three, and let Omega=(union F)\S have size six. If all three elements of S occur in strictly fewer than half the members of F, then B_6>=0 and therefore some element of Omega occurs in at least half the members.
claim_status: machine-checked candidate q=6 special-case theorem; not externally peer reviewed
